indicators: output reflects a shell command result
prerequisites: a field whose value reaches a shell
cheap_tests: append '; id' or '| id'
try newline and backtick variants
discriminating_tests: if spaces filtered, use ${IFS}: '|cat${IFS}/etc/flag.txt'
expected_observations: directory listing or command output appears below normal response
interpretation_rules: 'Invalid input'/filter message = filtered char, NOT 'no injection' — pivot separator/space encoding
no output but 200 = maybe blind; try time or out-of-band
common_mistakes: giving up when one metachar is blocked
failure_modes: WAF denylist blocks ; and spaced | (bypass with |, ${IFS}, $9)
recovery: swap separator (; | && || newline)
replace spaces with ${IFS}
read /etc/flag.txt and /tmp/flag.txt
verification: flag string appears in HTTP response body

prerequisites: user input rendered by a server template
cheap_tests: probe {{7*7}} -> expect 49
{{config}} to dump Flask config
discriminating_tests: {{lipsum.__globals__.os.popen('id').read()}} or {{cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen('id').read()}}
interpretation_rules: literal '{{7*7}}' echoed back = not evaluated (maybe different engine or escaped)
common_mistakes: assuming Jinja when it is Twig/Nunjucks — payload differs
recovery: read app source via popen('cat app.py'); flag/token often hardcoded there
verification: flag read from source or /flag via popen
examples: Status Page (TDHT) -> base64 flag in source [writeups/03]

technique: LFI / path traversal (incl. single-pass str_replace bypass)
indicators: ?path=/?file=/image loader with absolute path in page source
prerequisites: endpoint reads a file by user-controlled path
cheap_tests: ?path=/etc/flag.txt
read the handler itself: ?path=/var/www/html/image.php
discriminating_tests: if ../ stripped once, use '.....///' which collapses to ../ after one pass
php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php for source
interpretation_rules: filter that strips ../ only once is single-pass -> craft self-reforming sequence
common_mistakes: assuming recursive sanitization
recovery: prepend the required allowed prefix then traverse out
verification: flag file content in response

technique: Mass assignment / privilege escalation via extra field
indicators: JSON profile/update API returns a role field
prerequisites: update endpoint that binds request fields to the user object
cheap_tests: POST update with added '"role":"admin"'
discriminating_tests: re-fetch profile / hit /admin to confirm role changed
interpretation_rules: server silently accepting unknown fields = no allowlist
common_mistakes: overlooking commented JS that names the field
recovery: enumerate likely field names (role,is_admin,admin,privilege)
verification: flag on /admin page

prerequisites: client-side gate with no server validation
cheap_tests: fetch raw HTML/JS directly (bypasses devtools blocks)
read login.js/dashboard.js for the exact cookie checks
discriminating_tests: set cookies to required values, request protected page directly
interpretation_rules: string vs numeric equality matters ('10+1' != '11')
httpOnly blocks JS read but not always the gate
common_mistakes: fighting the anti-devtools layer instead of using raw HTTP
failure_modes: md5(role) cookie needs correct hash format 'admin|'+md5('admin')
recovery: forge the exact expected cookie value
verification: flag on the unlocked page

prerequisites: server that trusts header alg; published public key
cheap_tests: try alg:none first
forge HS256 signing with the JWK 'n' modulus STRING as HMAC secret
discriminating_tests: check /api/profile for token_role/is_admin flip
interpretation_rules: 'status:invalid' on alg:none -> try HS256 confusion, not give up
common_mistakes: using DER/PEM when server used the raw base64url n-string
recovery: also try PEM/DER/base64(DER)/modulus-bytes as HMAC key; or recover n via GCD of two sigs
verification: escalated endpoint returns admin-only data

indicators: HTML comments hint /redirect/?url= or worker port
prerequisites: server-side fetch of user URL; a naive host blocklist
cheap_tests: fetch http://example.com to confirm egress
try 127.0.0.1/localhost/169.254.169.254 (expect block)
discriminating_tests: bounce via app's own open redirect: /redirect/?url=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/
interpretation_rules: host string blocklist != IP-after-redirect check -> redirect bounce works
IMDSv2 needs PUT token -> GET-only SSRF is a dead end there
common_mistakes: marathon on 169.254.169.254 when only GET is possible
recovery: port-scan localhost via bounce; find non-framework internal worker
verification: internal secret/flag file read

technique: Time-based blind SQLi beating a response-time pad
indicators: result never echoed; die()==echo; response padded to fixed floor (e.g. 2.0s)
prerequisites: injection point that reaches SQL; SLEEP available
cheap_tests: calibrate: baseline vs '1 OR SLEEP(3)' vs a form that runs SLEEP regardless of rows
discriminating_tests: SLEEP(n) with n>pad so total ~= n; binary-search each flag char via IF(cond,SLEEP(n),0)
expected_observations: response time jumps above pad only when condition true
interpretation_rules: no delay != no SQLi: WHERE-clause SLEEP may not run (0 rows / short-circuit) -> change payload shape
fixed 2.0s floor kills sub-2s timing by design
common_mistakes: concluding 'DB broken/unsolvable' when SLEEP shows no delay (A1/A4 anti-pattern)
failure_modes: indexed single-row users -> '1 OR SLEEP' short-circuits
recovery: force SLEEP on every scanned row / UNION SELECT SLEEP; verify against known true/false first
verification: extracted flag chars reconstruct valid flag; ideally confirmed by submission

indicators: single-use action guarded by a read-then-write
prerequisites: endpoint with check-then-act on shared state
cheap_tests: fire N concurrent identical buys (asyncio/aiohttp or PowerShell runspaces)
discriminating_tests: observe balance/inventory going negative or item bought twice
expected_observations: more purchases succeed than balance should allow
interpretation_rules: intermittent success = timing window; increase concurrency/repeat
common_mistakes: sequential requests (never triggers the window)
recovery: raise concurrency; target the narrowest check-act pair
verification: flag returned after illegal state reached

indicators: JSON API takes an email/id string
changelog mentions a NEW feature (password reset, SMTP)
prerequisites: backend that iterates a value without type-checking
cheap_tests: send the field as an array: {"email":["victim@x","attacker@x"]}
discriminating_tests: check attacker mailbox for a NEW token addressed to victim
expected_observations: victim's reset token delivered to attacker-controlled address
interpretation_rules: identical success text for str/array can still hide different backend behavior -> check side effects (mailbox)
common_mistakes: only trying newline/comma SMTP header injection
recovery: also try comma-list, CC/BCC newline injection
verification: log in as victim with reset password; read flag on their dashboard

technique: Client-side flag reveal decoded in JS
indicators: reveal fn does NOT fetch a server
prerequisites: flag material embedded in client JS
cheap_tests: grep bundle for flag, TextDecoder, fromCharCode, ^ (xor), hex-array literals, _0x names
discriminating_tests: reproduce the local decode offline (seed often a tiny constant like state.length)
expected_observations: decode yields a coherent on-theme flag
interpretation_rules: the gate is usually a decoy — do NOT grind the intended task
common_mistakes: solving 10 timed math CAPTCHAs when the flag is computable offline
failure_modes: decode depends on server-provided value (then it is not fully client-side)
recovery: set completion state in console and call reveal fn; or breakpoint it
verification: byte-exact reproduction of the site's own decode = it IS the flag, not a guess

technique: XSS via input that is BOTH a valid jQuery selector AND valid JS eval
prerequisites: no CSP; jQuery 3.7.x; an admin bot that visits same-origin URLs
cheap_tests: build jsdom+real-jQuery harness; probe which chars/pseudos throw
discriminating_tests: payload x:eval(atob(document.forms.item(0).dataset.formula)) — label smuggles a real call; unknown :pseudo() don't throw and match nothing
interpretation_rules: selector must not throw AND return length 0 to reach eval branch
replaceState wipes #hash -> deliver code via query param/data-* not hash
common_mistakes: delivering payload in the hash (gets wiped)
recovery: validate whole flow locally, then fire ONE admin visit; exfil cookie to webhook
verification: admin cookie token=K17{...} arrives at collector

technique: Cookie shadowing/tossing -> same-origin XSS to read httpOnly flag
indicators: same cookie rendered UNescaped on an authed page
XSS bot logs in and visits reported URL
prerequisites: one unescaped sink; ability to set a same-name cookie at a more specific path
cheap_tests: identify the single unescaped template sink among escaped ones
discriminating_tests: set FLAG cookie at path=/admin with an XSS payload; bot loads /admin -> executes
expected_observations: payload runs on app origin as authed admin
interpretation_rules: httpOnly blocks JS READ, not creating another cookie of same name/other path
more specific path wins on that path
common_mistakes: concluding 'no XSS found' and stopping
recovery: delete own /admin cookie, refetch /admin so real httpOnly flag renders, exfil
verification: real flag exfiltrated to attacker webhook

prerequisites: merge into an object whose props gate auth/behavior
cheap_tests: POST {"__proto__":{"isAdmin":true}} or array-path variant to bypass WAF
discriminating_tests: check a subsequent request honors the polluted prop
interpretation_rules: sticky node/instance may be required (pollution is per-process)
common_mistakes: polluting the wrong prototype/instance
recovery: try {"path":["__proto__","x"],"value":...} array form to dodge key filters
verification: /api/flag or admin path returns flag

indicators: terminal returns constant '0x00' for normal commands
flavor hint about reading 'ball by ball' / character-by-character
prerequisites: server decodes input by an undocumented per-char rule
cheap_tests: send normal cmds and note uniform non-answer
take the flavor hint LITERALLY as the mechanism
discriminating_tests: reconstruct formula repeat=((ord%5)+3)+(pos%3); encode 'cat flag.txt'; verify decoder locally
expected_observations: encoded blob decodes server-side to a real command; flag returned
interpretation_rules: anti-debug (F12 block/debugger loops) here was pure decoy — ignore it
implement+verify the decoder locally before spamming the server
common_mistakes: chasing command-injection/rate-limit when it was an encoding puzzle
recovery: adjust formula params against known-good round-trips
verification: server returns Kaal{...}

prerequisites: short ciphertext, one key byte
cheap_tests: XOR every byte with all 256 keys, keep printable
discriminating_tests: one key yields clean ASCII (e.g. VIBRANIUM-######)
interpretation_rules: per-instance ciphertext changes but pipeline is constant -> automate connect/decode/reply
common_mistakes: not automating the single netcat session
recovery: fall back to known-plaintext crib drag
verification: service accepts plaintext and returns flag

indicators: short token; letters-only or base32/base64 alphabet; L...{-shaped strings
prerequisites: known/guessable classical transform
cheap_tests: auto-try: Caesar 25 shifts, ROT13, ROT47, Atbash, b64->b32, hex-decode then reverse
discriminating_tests: the transform that yields the flag prefix (CHAKRA{/Kaal{/etc.)
interpretation_rules: flag NAME often names the cipher (p1_atbash, p1_caesar) — trust it
decoys are ROT13 too and announce themselves ('honeypot','N0TH1NG')
common_mistakes: submitting a decoy entry
recovery: peel layers in reverse; try both orderings
verification: prefix matches required format and text is coherent
examples: Mirror Dimension atbash, SHIELD b64->b32, I Am Groot hex+reverse, Server's Secret ROT13 [writeups/10-15]

indicators: sign(m)=popcount(row & m)%2 per row / matrix*vector / XOR-folds
NO nonce, NO nonlinear step (no S-box/modadd/hash)
oracle signs chosen msgs + a free sign(user), blocks only signing target 'root'
prerequisites: linearity: sign(0)=0, sign(a^b)=sign(a)^sign(b)
cheap_tests: locally prove sign(a^b)=sign(a)^sign(b) on 1000 random keys
discriminating_tests: query q=root^user (!=root), then sign(root)=sign(q)^sign(user)
interpretation_rules: absence of nonce+nonlinearity => linear => forgeable without key
common_mistakes: trying to recover the matrix instead of exploiting linearity
failure_modes: any nonlinear step breaks the identity
recovery: general case: query a basis, solve the linear system for target
verification: server accepts forged tag (self-validating)

prerequisites: RSA parameters
cheap_tests: factordb / sympy.factorint on n; try RsaCtfTool first
discriminating_tests: e=3 & small m -> integer cube root (gmpy2.iroot)
p~q -> Fermat
shared factor gcd(n,c) or gcd(n1,n2)
small d -> Wiener/Boneh-Durfee
same m diff e same n -> common-modulus Bezout
Hastad broadcast e=3 across 3 (n,c) -> CRT + cube root
interpretation_rules: pick the branch by what is leaked; do not brute a strong modulus
common_mistakes: running generic tools on a modulus that needs a specific attack
recovery: install gmpy2 or use container-equivalent; fall back to pure-python where possible
verification: decrypted bytes contain flag format

technique: Groth16 proof forgery from leaked toxic waste (tau)
indicators: ZK verifier + 'ceremony/ashes/secret not hidden well enough'
tarball with bellman/pairing (BLS12-381), vk.bin, a 'secret' file
prerequisites: tau (toxic waste) recoverable (often ROT13/obfuscated)
cheap_tests: ROT13 the secret file -> CEREMONY_ID + TAU
derive [alpha,beta,gamma,delta,s1,s2] from tau (blake2b expand)
discriminating_tests: dump vk.bin; confirm SCALED generators (G1base=s1*G1, G2base=s2*G2) before assuming textbook layout
expected_observations: local verify() returns true for forged (A,B,C)
interpretation_rules: circuit constraints irrelevant — construct A/B/C to satisfy pairing, no witness
common_mistakes: assuming standard generators; not verifying vk elements
failure_modes: Windows: needs stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu toolchain (no MSVC linker)
recovery: reuse challenge's own derive/g1/g2/verify; set A=alpha_g1,B=beta_g2; C=-(ic0+claim*ic1)*s1*gamma/delta
verification: server responds 'accepted' + flag

indicators: telemetry/heartbeat feed; perfectly regular payload clock
prerequisites: pcap with capture timestamps + in-payload device timestamps
cheap_tests: per-entity delay = capture_ts - device_ts; stats (mean/std/max)
discriminating_tests: histogram delays for trimodal bands; find provably-empty dead zone; look for byte-aligned magic (e.g. TRP1)
expected_observations: carriers breach stated tolerance; magic lands at bit 0; length field balances; checksum validates
interpretation_rules: a perfect metronome payload clock = null channel; signal is in what sender can't fake (arrival time)
if you must TUNE a threshold to get printable output, you're overfitting
common_mistakes: modelling val/us-ts (payload gravity); chasing decoy carriers without the magic anchor
failure_modes: multiple decoy carriers decode to junk
recovery: use magic+length+checksum triple self-check; key from first-N calibration bytes in registration order
verification: AES-CTR->zlib->JSON with valid Adler-32 yields flag

indicators: artifact ships BOTH packaged and pre-extracted
prerequisites: OOXML zip; oletools
cheap_tests: DIFF packaged vs extracted FIRST (localizes author edits)
unzip, inspect xl/macrosheets + docProps/core.xml
discriminating_tests: core.xml creator/lastModifiedBy often carry the payload; 'synt'=ROT13('flag')
interpretation_rules: flag may NOT be in macro semantics — check metadata/strings
match EXACT required case (flag{} vs FLAG{})
common_mistakes: reversing macro C2 logic while flag sits in core.xml; running diff LAST
failure_modes: exact accepted format ambiguous without validator
recovery: present all format variants in ONE message; ask for oracle
verification: ROT13 round-trip is byte-exact; ideally platform-confirmed
examples: Phish to Fortune -> flag{y0u F0und 0s} (format unconfirmed) [TRAINING_NOTES #22]

indicators: image or wav handout with no obvious content
'the image speaks when bytes align' style hint
prerequisites: PIL/numpy (native) or zsteg/steghide (container-only)
cheap_tests: exiftool/strings first; then R/G/B LSB row-scan -> often base64
for wav: render spectrogram (text in frequency domain)
discriminating_tests: LSB bytes base64-decode to flag; ICMT comment = zip password
expected_observations: decoded base64 -> CHAKRA{}/Kaal{} flag; or text drawn in spectrogram
interpretation_rules: uniform LSB across all bytes = probably NOT the channel
common_mistakes: reaching for zsteg/steghide which are container-only (Docker deleted)
failure_modes: steghide needs a passphrase (try challenge nickname/theme)
recovery: bitplane split; check data after IEND / after ZIP EOCD; fix RIFX/RIFF header
verification: decoded flag matches format

technique: Off-by-one / local-variable aliasing stack pwn (index escape)
indicators: struct/buffer with sibling scalars (counter, accumulator, win flag)
loop counter can be nudged past its bound (double-increment/skip)
prerequisites: source or objdump to map local offsets to array indices
cheap_tests: map objdump offsets: which locals alias numbers[i]; where is win vs array
discriminating_tests: set counter itself via OOB write; reach field BELOW array at negative index
expected_observations: win flag cleared / control reached without ret overwrite
interpretation_rules: target may be reachable at a negative index instead of via return address (dodges canary)
common_mistakes: assuming return-address overwrite is the only path
recovery: simulate signed-correct behavior locally; confirm on local -no-pie build before remote
verification: win() prints /flag remotely

technique: Predictable-RNG reconnect brute (one lucky event suffices)
indicators: one win with a large stake leaps a comparison threshold; losing ends session cleanly
prerequisites: cheap reconnects; win probability like 1/36
cheap_tests: compute stake so a single win crosses threshold w/o int overflow (2*wager<INT_MAX)
discriminating_tests: reconnect until first spin wins (~36 tries)
interpretation_rules: retry-friendly rare event -> brute beats modelling the PRNG
an 'arbitrary write' gated by addr<=&stackvar can't reach vars ABOVE it in caller frames
common_mistakes: predicting the PRNG seed unnecessarily
recovery: automate connect/try/close loop until flag appears
verification: server runs win() and prints flag

indicators: input length gate then a folded hash compare
prerequisites: capstone+unicorn (native) to emulate; patience
cheap_tests: decrypt runtime blob (often LCG keystream) to recover S-box + program
discriminating_tests: re-derive EVERY opcode/handler byte-by-byte; emulate real binary vs python model on random inputs
expected_observations: python model matches binary hash on 200/200 inputs
interpretation_rules: matching random outputs proves emulation, NOT understanding of the intended check
if the gate is only a 32-bit hash over free bytes -> collisions exist -> if unique flag expected, your assumption is wrong; keep digging (don't submit a collision)
common_mistakes: presenting a constructed collision as 'the flag'; declaring 'underdetermined/flawed'
failure_modes: no per-step oracle found -> flag not uniquely pinned from binary alone
recovery: hunt a stronger constraint (store-with-no-load handler); question the input-format assumption; ask for grading model
verification: only accept a self-validating or platform-accepted flag

technique: Pickle deserialization jail (omit STOP to crash the disassembler check)
indicators: bans byte-substrings + bans REDUCE via pickletools.dis() text
restricted find_class allowlist; output = redirected stdout
prerequisites: can send raw pickle bytes
cheap_tests: note STOP opcode is '.' (0x2e) which is banned -> a normal pickle is rejected
discriminating_tests: omit STOP -> dis() raises -> except:pass sets disassembled='Error!' -> REDUCE ban bypassed; load() still executes opcodes as read
interpretation_rules: banning an opcode STRING from a disassembler -> make the disassembler crash (except:pass = silent bypass)
reach builtins via allowed module __builtins__ dict + operator.itemgetter (collections._itemgetter)
common_mistakes: writing 'c collections' (space) -> module lookup fails; include STOP -> rejected
failure_modes: strict opcode allowlist on the unpickler
recovery: \xNN-escaped protocol-0 STRING to hide banned bytes (flag,.)
verification: flag file contents printed in output

indicators: eval() of user input with regex filter banning () " ' digits, limited builtins
prerequisites: reachable dangerous dunder OR a Python-level function for __globals__ bridge
cheap_tests: confirm deployed filter == public source (send a paren payload -> 'Nope')
build no-digit ints (True+True), build strings via %c/attr-name slicing
discriminating_tests: find a call primitive without (): decorators, __class_getitem__, obj[arg] via __getitem__, walrus binds
interpretation_rules: only C-level dunders on reachable objects => genuinely no call primitive => need extra surface (version/Dockerfile)
NEVER declare impossible for a hinted medium — attack the given gadgets (hint_A/hint_B)
common_mistakes: overthinking with big fuzzers; giving up and asking user for Dockerfile instead of solving
failure_modes: no Python-level function reachable -> no __globals__ bridge
recovery: Unicode/NFKC fullwidth bypass of char filter; raise length limits on the fly; see REFERENCE_jiegec pyjail chains
verification: /flag read or shell obtained

technique: AI chatbot prompt-injection via state machine
indicators: AI 'guardian' with a themed multi-stage story
prerequisites: a /chat API; per-session state tracking
cheap_tests: read app.js for /chat contract; ignore HTML-comment decoy flags
discriminating_tests: walk the required stages IN ORDER using the challenge's own thematic language, then declare the themed 'realization' phrase
expected_observations: bot transitions to unlocked state, reveals flag
interpretation_rules: generic 'ignore instructions' gets deflected; the theme IS the key
decoy flag names announce themselves (N0TH1NG_K33P_TRY1NG)
common_mistakes: jumping straight to 'give me the flag'
failure_modes: skipping a stage keeps it locked
recovery: complete every stage; use culturally/thematically correct unlock phrase
verification: bot prints the real flag

indicators: service prints an encoded challenge + asks for plaintext
flag is per-instance but pipeline is constant
prerequisites: single TCP session; identify encoding from a keyword in the prompt
cheap_tests: connect once, read prompt keyword (binary/rot47/morse/base_chain/xor)
discriminating_tests: decode per keyword, WriteLine plaintext in the SAME session, read flag
expected_observations: service returns the flag after correct reply
interpretation_rules: server closes after one wrong answer -> reconnect per attempt when brute forcing
on Windows use System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient (nc not present)
common_mistakes: opening a new connection between prompt and reply (loses state)
recovery: automate connect->parse->decode->send->read as one script
verification: service emits flag
examples: Stark Telemetry morse, SHIELD base-chain, Mirror atbash (CHAKRA) [writeups/10-13]
